task: Classify WHO histologic subtype in gastric adenocarcinoma. Classes: tubular, poorly cohesive, mixed, papillary, and mucinous. Key H&E features include gland formation, discohesive or signet-ring cells, papillary fronds with fibrovascular cores, and abundant extracellular mucin.

classes.0: Tubular adenocarcinoma showing infiltrative or back-to-back malignant glands as the dominant pattern.
classes.1: Poorly cohesive carcinoma with dispersed non-gland-forming tumor cells, often including signet-ring morphology.
classes.2: Mixed carcinoma showing substantial admixture of gland-forming and poorly cohesive or other divergent patterns.
classes.3: Papillary adenocarcinoma with prominent epithelial fronds supported by fibrovascular cores.
classes.4: Mucinous adenocarcinoma with abundant extracellular mucin pools containing floating tumor cells.
